original.guitar: David and Howard Bellamy, Richard Bennett and Doug Rhone (per MusicBrainz credits)
original.amp: Not documented. Mid-70s LA studio sound: clean Fender-style amp
original.effects: Light compression, delay, studio plate reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: Recorded October 1975 at Wally Heider Recording Studio, Hollywood; produced by Phil Gernhard and Tony Scotti; single released 1976. Written by Larry Williams.

recipes.tips: Channel A for clean, bright fills and arpeggios over the acoustic strumming. Channel B is a warmer AC15 with a touch of grit for melodic lines and a solo. Keep the playing light and let the notes ring: the song floats, it doesn't push. For the strummed acoustic part, switch to LOVE AC.
recipes.why: Mid-70s LA soft-rock and country-pop records used a clean Fender-style electric, lightly compressed, with a short delay and a studio plate reverb. Both pickups, split, give a glassy, Strat-like middle-position sound.

Goldmine: The Bellamy Brothers celebrate their 50th anniversary

original.guitar: David and Howard Bellamy on guitar (per MusicBrainz credits); acoustic-driven arrangement
original.effects: Studio plate reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: Recorded October 1975 at Wally Heider Recording Studio, Hollywood; single released 1976.

recipes.tips: The song is built on strummed acoustic guitar. The ACOUSTIC effect in the PEDAL slot makes the Tele sound like one. Channel A is warmer, channel B brighter. Strum lightly and evenly. Stomp MOD for a gentle stereo chorus, a 70s touch. Turn PEDAL off for a plain clean electric. For fills, switch to LOVE CL.
recipes.why: If there's no acoustic player in the band, an acoustic simulation into a very clean amp covers the song's main part. Split pickups in the middle position give the least electric-sounding source for the simulation, and a plate reverb gives the 70s studio space.
